summary: Usually an oath lets a person avoid paying. But in some cases the person claiming swears and gets paid: a hired worker, someone who was robbed, someone who was hurt, and more. Rabbi Yehudah says the other side must first admit part of it.

chunks.en: Everyone who swears an oath from the Torah
chunks.st: All those who take an oath that is legislated by the Torah

chunks.en: swears so he does not have to pay.
chunks.st: take an oath and do not pay.
chunks.stMore: By Torah law, one takes an oath only in order to exempt himself from a monetary claim.

chunks.en: But these people swear and take the money:
chunks.st: And these litigants take a rabbinically instituted oath and receive
chunks.stMore: possession of the disputed funds or property, i.e., their claim is upheld by means of the oath, even though they are not in possession of the property in question:

chunks.en: a hired worker, one who was robbed,
chunks.st: A hired worker who claims that he has not received his wages; and one who was robbed and sues the person who robbed him;

chunks.en: one who was hurt, and one whose opponent is not trusted to swear,
chunks.st: and one who was injured, who claims compensation from the person who injured him; and one whose opposing litigant is suspect with regard to the taking of an oath.
chunks.stMore: When a person suspected of taking false oaths is liable to take an oath in order to exempt himself, the claimant takes an oath instead and receives payment.

chunks.en: and a storekeeper with his notebook.
chunks.st: And a storekeeper relying on his ledger also takes an oath and is paid.

chunks.st: my wages that are still in your possession.

chunks.en: the boss says, "I gave it,"
chunks.st: The employer says: I already gave them to you.

chunks.en: and the worker says, "I did not get it,"
chunks.st: And that worker says: I have not received them.

chunks.en: the worker swears and takes his pay.
chunks.st: In such a case, the worker takes an oath that he has not received his wages, and he receives payment from his employer.

chunks.en: Rabbi Yehudah says,
chunks.st: Rabbi Yehuda says: This oath cannot be administered

chunks.en: only if the boss admits part of it.
chunks.st: unless there is partial admission on the part of the employer.

chunks.he: כֵּיצַד, אָמַר לוֹ תֶּן לִי שְׂכָרִי
chunks.en: How so? He said to him, "Give me my pay,
chunks.st: How so? The case is where the worker said to him: Give me my wages,

chunks.en: fifty dinar that you still have,"
chunks.st: fifty silver dinars, which are still in your possession.

chunks.en: and the boss says, "You already got a gold dinar."
chunks.explain: A gold dinar is worth twenty-five, so he admitted part.
chunks.st: And the employer says: You have already received one golden dinar, which is worth twenty-five silver dinars.
chunks.stMore: Since the employer has admitted that he owes part of the sum, the worker takes an oath and is paid the whole sum.

summary: How does it work with someone who was robbed? Witnesses saw the other man go into his house to take a mashkon without permission. He swears about what was taken and gets paid.

chunks.en: How does it work with one who was robbed?
chunks.st: How does this halakha apply to one who was robbed?

chunks.en: Witnesses said that he went
chunks.st: The case is where witnesses testified about the defendant that he entered

chunks.en: into his house to take a mashkon without permission,
chunks.st: the claimant’s house to seize collateral from him without the authority to do so.

words.en: to take a mashkon from him

chunks.en: and he says, "You took my things,"
chunks.st: The claimant said: You took items that belong to me.

chunks.en: and the other says, "I did not take them,"
chunks.st: And the defendant said: I did not take them.

chunks.en: this one swears and takes payment.
chunks.st: The claimant takes an oath and receives payment of his claim.

chunks.en: Rabbi Yehudah says,
chunks.st: Rabbi Yehuda says: This oath cannot be administered

chunks.en: only if the other admits part of it.
chunks.st: unless there is partial admission on the part of the defendant.

chunks.he: כֵּיצַד, אָמַר לוֹ שְׁנֵי כֵלִים נָטַלְתָּ,
chunks.en: How so? He said to him, "You took two things,"
chunks.st: How so? The case is where the claimant said to him: You took two items.

chunks.he: וְהוּא אוֹמֵר לֹא נָטַלְתִּי אֶלָּא אֶחָד:

chunks.st: And he says: I took only one.
chunks.stMore: Since the defendant admits that he took one item from the house, the claimant takes an oath and receives payment of his whole claim.

summary: How does it work with someone who was hurt? Witnesses saw him go into the other man's place healthy and come out hurt. He swears and gets paid.

chunks.en: How does it work with one who was hurt?
chunks.st: How does this halakha apply to one who was injured?

chunks.en: Witnesses said that he went into the other's place
chunks.st: The case is where witnesses testified about the injured person that he entered into the domain of

chunks.en: healthy, and came out hurt,
chunks.st: the defendant whole but left injured,

chunks.en: and he said to him, "You hurt me,"
chunks.st: and the claimant said to the defendant: You injured me.

chunks.en: and the other says, "I did not hurt you,"
chunks.st: And the defendant says: I did not injure you.

chunks.en: this one swears and takes payment.
chunks.st: The injured party takes an oath and receives compensation.

chunks.en: Rabbi Yehudah says,
chunks.st: Rabbi Yehuda says: This oath cannot be administered

chunks.en: only if the other admits part of it.
chunks.st: unless there is partial admission.

chunks.he: כֵּיצַד, אָמַר לוֹ חָבַלְתָּ בִּי שְׁתַּיִם,
chunks.en: How so? He said to him, "You hurt me twice,"
chunks.st: How so? The case is where the claimant said to the defendant: You injured me twice.

chunks.en: and the other says, "I hurt you
chunks.st: And the other says: I injured

chunks.en: only once."
chunks.st: you only once.
chunks.stMore: In such a case, the injured party takes an oath that he was injured twice and receives compensation for both injuries.

summary: If one side is not trusted to swear, because he swore falsely before or earns money in a forbidden way, the other side swears and takes the money. If neither can be trusted, Rabbi Yosei and Rabbi Meir argue what to do.

chunks.en: How does it work when the other side is not trusted to swear?
chunks.st: How does this halakha apply to one whose opposing litigant is suspect with regard to the taking of an oath and therefore is not permitted to take the oath?

chunks.he: אַחַת שְׁבוּעַת הָעֵדוּת וְאַחַת שְׁבוּעַת הַפִּקָּדוֹן,
chunks.en: If he swore falsely before, whether a shevuas ha'eidus or a shevuas hapikadon,
chunks.st: One is considered suspect with regard to oaths if he has been found to have taken a false oath, whether it was an oath of testimony, or whether it was an oath on a deposit,

chunks.en: or even a shevuas shav.
chunks.st: or even an oath taken in vain, which is a less severe prohibition.
chunks.stMore: There are also categories of people who by rabbinic decree are considered suspect with regard to oaths:

chunks.en: If one of them plays dice for money,
chunks.st: If one of the litigants was a dice player,

chunks.en: or lends with ribbis,
chunks.st: or one who lends with interest, or

words.note: Interest: extra money for a loan, which the Torah forbids.

chunks.en: or races pigeons,
chunks.st: among those who fly pigeons, or

chunks.en: or does business with Shemittah produce,
chunks.st: among the vendors of produce of the Sabbatical Year,

words.note: Fruit of the seventh year, which may not be used for business.

chunks.en: then the other side swears and takes the money.
chunks.explain: The Sages do not trust such people to swear.
chunks.st: then the litigant opposing him takes an oath and receives payment of his claim.

chunks.en: If both of them are not trusted,
chunks.st: If both litigants were suspect,

chunks.en: the oath goes back to its place.
chunks.explain: The Gemara explains what this means.
chunks.st: the oath returned to its place.

chunks.en: These are the words of Rabbi Yosei.
chunks.st: This is the statement of Rabbi Yosei, and will be explained in the Gemara.

chunks.en: Rabbi Meir says, they split it.
chunks.st: Rabbi Meir says: Since neither can take an oath, they divide the disputed amount.

summary: A storekeeper was told to give things to someone's son or workers, and they say they never got them. Both swear and get paid. Ben Nanas says both get paid without an oath, so that no one swears falsely.

chunks.en: How does it work with a storekeeper and his notebook?
chunks.st: And how does this halakha apply to the storekeeper relying on his ledger?

chunks.he: לֹא שֶׁיֹּאמַר לוֹ כָּתוּב עַל פִּנְקָסִי
chunks.en: Not when he says, "It is written in my notebook
chunks.st: This ruling is not referring to the case where a storekeeper says to a customer: It is written in my ledger

chunks.en: that you owe me two hundred zuz,"
chunks.st: that you owe me two hundred dinars.

chunks.en: but when the customer told him, "Give
chunks.st: Rather, it is referring to a case where a customer says to a storekeeper: Give

chunks.en: my son two se'ah of wheat,"
chunks.st: my son two se’a of wheat, or:

chunks.en: or "Give my workers a sela in coins,"
chunks.st: Give my laborers a sela in small coins.

chunks.en: the storekeeper says, "I gave it," and they
chunks.st: And later the storekeeper says: I gave it to them; but they say:

chunks.en: say, "We did not get it" (both of them swear):
chunks.st: We did not receive it.

chunks.en: the storekeeper swears and gets paid,
chunks.st: In such a case, where the father or employer admits that he gave those instructions and it is also recorded in the storekeeper’s ledger, the storekeeper takes an oath that he gave the son the wheat or paid the laborers, and he receives compensation from the father or employer;

chunks.en: and the workers swear and get paid.
chunks.explain: The boss has to pay both of them.
chunks.st: and the laborers take an oath that they were not paid and receive their wages from the employer.

chunks.en: Ben Nanas said,
chunks.st: Ben Nannas said:

chunks.he: כֵּיצַד אֵלּוּ בָאִין לִידֵי שְׁבוּעַת שָׁוְא
chunks.en: How can these come to a false oath,
chunks.st: How is it that both these and those come to take an oath in vain?

chunks.en: and those come to a false oath?
chunks.explain: One of them must be lying.
chunks.st: One of them is certainly lying.

chunks.en: Rather, the storekeeper gets paid without an oath,
chunks.st: Rather, the storekeeper receives his compensation without taking an oath,

chunks.en: and the workers get paid without an oath.
chunks.st: and the laborers receive their wages without taking an oath.

summary: A storekeeper or money changer and a customer argue about who already paid. The one being asked to pay swears. Rabbi Yehudah says the one holding the goods wins.

chunks.st: If one said to a storekeeper: Give me

chunks.st: And later the storekeeper said to him: Give me that dinar you owe me,

chunks.en: If he gave him the dinar,
chunks.st: If, after he gave the storekeeper the money, the customer

chunks.st: and you transported it to your house,

chunks.st: Rabbi Yehuda says:

chunks.st: Whoever has the produce in his possession

chunks.st: and subsequently the money changer said to him: Give me the dinar,

chunks.en: and he said, "I gave it to you, and you put it in your wallet,"
chunks.st: and the customer said to him: I gave it to you, and you put it in your wallet;

chunks.en: Rabbi Yehudah says,
chunks.st: Rabbi Yehuda says:

summary: More cases where someone must swear before collecting money: a woman collecting her kesubah in certain cases, and orphans collecting a loan that was owed to their father.

chunks.en: Just as the Sages said:
chunks.st: These cases of taking an oath are just like other cases where the Sages said that one takes an oath and receives payment.

chunks.he: הַפּוֹגֶמֶת כְּתֻבָּתָהּ לֹא תִפָּרַע אֶלָּא בִשְׁבוּעָה,
chunks.en: A woman who admits she got part of her kesubah can collect the rest only with an oath,
chunks.st: A woman who vitiates her marriage contract by acknowledging receipt of partial payment may collect the remainder only by taking an oath; or

words.note: The money a husband promises his wife in her kesubah.

chunks.en: and if one witness says that it was paid,
chunks.st: if one witness testifies that her marriage contract has been paid,

chunks.en: she can collect only with an oath.
chunks.st: she may collect it only by taking an oath.

chunks.en: From property that was sold to others, or from orphans' property,
chunks.st: She may collect it from liened property that has been sold to a third party, or from the property of orphans,

chunks.en: she can collect only with an oath.
chunks.st: only by taking an oath,

chunks.en: And a woman who collects when her husband is not there
chunks.st: and a woman who collects it from her husband’s property when not in his presence

chunks.en: can collect only with an oath.
chunks.st: may collect it only by taking an oath.

chunks.he: וְכֵן הַיְתוֹמִים לֹא יִפָּרְעוּ אֶלָּא בִשְׁבוּעָה,
chunks.en: And orphans too can collect a loan only with an oath:
chunks.st: And likewise, orphans may collect a loan with a promissory note inherited from their father only by taking an oath.
chunks.stMore: Orphans who wish to collect payment of money owed to their father must take the following oath:

chunks.en: "We swear that Abba did not tell us before he died,
chunks.st: On our oath our father did not direct us on his deathbed not to collect with this promissory note,

chunks.en: and Abba did not tell us that it was paid,
chunks.st: and our father did not say to us that this note was paid,

chunks.en: and we did not find among the papers of
chunks.st: and we did not find among our father’s documents

chunks.en: Abba that this loan paper was paid."
chunks.st: a record showing that this promissory note was paid. After taking that oath, they may collect the money.

chunks.en: Rabbi Yochanan ben Beroka says,
chunks.st: Rabbi Yoḥanan ben Beroka says:

chunks.he: אֲפִלּוּ נוֹלַד הַבֵּן לְאַחַר מִיתַת הָאָב,
chunks.en: Even if the son was born after the father died,
chunks.st: Even if the son was born after the father’s death,

chunks.en: he swears and takes it.
chunks.st: he needs to take an oath in order to receive the money owed to his father.

chunks.en: Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel said,
chunks.st: Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel said:

chunks.he: אִם יֵשׁ עֵדִים שֶׁאָמַר הָאָב בִּשְׁעַת
chunks.en: If there are witnesses that the father said when he was dying,
chunks.st: If there are witnesses that the father said at the time

chunks.en: "This loan paper has not been paid,"
chunks.st: of his death: This promissory note has not been paid,

chunks.en: the son takes it without an oath.
chunks.st: the son collects the debt without having to take an oath.

summary: Partners, sharecroppers and people who handle other people's things must swear even without a clear claim. An oath for one thing can be rolled over to include other claims too.

chunks.en: These people must swear even without a clear claim:
chunks.st: And these people are sometimes required to take an oath that they do not owe anything even when there is no explicit claim against them:

chunks.en: partners, sharecroppers,
chunks.st: Partners, sharecroppers,

words.note: An aris works someone's field for part of the crop.

chunks.he: וְהָאַפּוֹטְרוֹפִּין, וְהָאִשָּׁה הַנּוֹשֵׂאת וְהַנּוֹתֶנֶת בְּתוֹךְ הַבַּיִת,
chunks.en: guardians, a woman who runs the business of the house,
chunks.st: stewards [apotropin], a woman who does business from home, where she manages the property of orphans,

words.note: An apotropos takes care of orphans' property.

chunks.en: and a member of the household.
chunks.explain: Someone put in charge of the family's things.
chunks.st: and the member of the household appointed to manage the household’s affairs.

chunks.en: If he said, "What is your claim against me?"
chunks.st: For example, in a case where one of these people said to one of the people whose property he or she manages: What is your claim against me? If the other replied:

chunks.en: and the other said, "I just want you to swear to me,"
chunks.st: It is simply my wish that you take an oath to me that you have not taken anything of mine,

chunks.en: he must swear.
chunks.st: the former is liable to take that oath.

chunks.en: Once the partners or sharecroppers have divided,
chunks.st: Once the partners or the sharecroppers have divided the common property, each taking his share,

chunks.en: one cannot make the other swear.
chunks.st: then one side may not require an oath of the other absent a definite claim.

chunks.en: But if he has to swear for some other reason,
chunks.st: But if an oath was imposed upon him due to some other situation,

chunks.en: we can roll everything into that oath.
chunks.st: that oath can be extended to impose upon him any
chunks.stMore: other oath, i.e., it can be extended to apply to any other of their disputes. The mishna adds:

chunks.en: And the Shemittah year cancels the oath.
chunks.explain: Just as Shemittah cancels a loan.
chunks.st: And the Sabbatical Year abrogates the obligation to take an oath about a debt, just like it abrogates a debt.
